page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor operating at 3.2 GHz, delivering 12 virtual CPUs across 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and network-based resources. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 8624.76 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5654.0. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1149.99. Memory performance shows a clear asymmetry: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 620.37 GB/sec, large-block uncached write bandwidth is weak at 24.54 GB/sec. The instance handles lightweight workloads like Redis SET operations (9.94 million operations per second) and static web serving (9.12 GB/sec) with average efficiency, but struggles with more demanding tasks, showing weak performance in medium 7B LLM inference.

Given its compute-oriented vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1:2, the ecs.c4.3xlarge offers a balanced entry point for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a cost-efficient option for stateless applications, web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations. It is best suited for multi-threaded applications, CI/CD pipelines, and general-purpose web servers that can leverage its 12 dedicated vCPUs without hitting memory or storage bottlenecks.
